hook: Ask someone in the United States to name a nation and they will probably name a country. A geographer means something different. The Kurds, a people of tens of millions in Southwest Asia, share a language, history and homeland, yet they have no country of their own. Iceland is a country where almost everyone shares one culture. Nigeria is one country holding hundreds of peoples. Political geography starts by pulling apart two words: nation and state.

prereq.q: What is culture, as geographers use the word?
options: The shared beliefs, practices and traits of a group of people
The physical landscape of a region
The number of people in a place
prereq.why: Culture is the shared way of life of a group: language, religion, customs, food and more.

options: People who share an ancestry and cultural traits such as language or religion
People who live in the same city
People who hold the same job
prereq.why: Ethnicity is a cultural identity built on shared ancestry, language, religion and customs.

figure.caption: Four ways nations (peoples) and states (countries) fit together.

chain.cause: A group of people shares a language, history and homeland
chain.effect: they see themselves as one nation

chain.cause: That nation wants to run its own affairs
chain.effect: it seeks a state of its own, or powers inside an existing state

chain.cause: State borders rarely match where nations live
chain.effect: many states hold several nations, and some nations have no state

ideas: A state is a country: a permanent population, a defined territory, a government that controls it, and recognition by other states. A nation is a people who share a culture and see themselves as one.
A nation-state is one nation in one state (Iceland comes close). A multinational state holds several nations (Nigeria, Belgium).
A multistate nation lives in two or more states (Koreans). A stateless nation has no state of its own (the Kurds).
An autonomous region governs many of its own affairs inside a state: Greenland in the Kingdom of Denmark, the Kurdistan Region in Iraq, Native American reservations in the United States.

misconception.wrong: A nation and a state are the same thing: both just mean a country.
misconception.right: A nation is a people; a state is a country with a government. The Kurds are a nation with no state, and Nigeria is one state with many nations.

summary: States are the basic political units of the world: each has people, territory, a government and recognition by other states. Nations are peoples who share a culture. When one nation fills one state, the result is a nation-state; most states are multinational, some nations live in several states, and some, such as the Kurds, have no state at all. Autonomous regions govern many of their own affairs inside a larger state.
